messages:
Isabella Rossi: Heads up on a long-context edge case from microbench: our H100 `attn_sm90_v3` fallback condition is disabling v3 *even when requests are short*, if the model advertises `max_seq_len` > 8192.

Example: llama-3-70b-32k (rope scaled) -> we pick v2 at model load b/c `model.max_seqlen=32768`, even if actual prefill is 2k/4k most of the time.

I think our gate is too conservative / wrong signal.

Grace Kim: wait, we’re gating on `model_max_seq_len`? I thought it was runtime `prefill_len`.

Isabella Rossi: looks like both depending on codepath. In my branch (pulled from `kernel-v3-sticky`), the “sticky choose at model init” path uses `model_config.max_position_embeddings` and bails out if >8192.

So any 16k/32k model = v3 never used.

Hiro Tanaka: ugh, that’s not intended. The original concern was v3 stability for *actual* very long prefill (and mixed batches), not the model’s theoretical max.

Noah Patel: +1. Gating on model max is going to penalize anyone shipping long-context models w/ mostly normal traffic.

If we change to per-request gating we reintroduce the p99 jitter issue though.

Yuki Sato: right, sticky is good for tail. but we can do sticky “default=v3” + a per-request *hard* fallback only when `prefill_len > threshold` (or `batch_max_prefill > threshold`).

That way 32k model still uses v3 for 2-8k traffic.

Grace Kim: that makes sense. We need to be careful with batching: if one 12k request gets batched with others, `batch_max_prefill` will trip and whole batch falls back.

Isabella Rossi: exactly. I can reproduce the badness with a mixed distribution.

Harness:
- GPU: h100-sxm, CUDA 12.4, driver 550.54
- model: llama3-70b-32k (fp16)
- concurrency=16
- prefill lens sampled: {1024, 2048, 4096, 12288} weights {0.45, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10}
- decode=64

When sticky gate uses model max -> v2 100% (stable but slower)
When sticky default=v3 + per-batch fallback @8192 -> v3 chosen ~86% of batches but p99 gets spiky when 12k requests show up and cause fallback for big mixed batches.

Marcus Reed: can you paste p99 numbers? trying to understand magnitude.

Isabella Rossi: sure (request latency ms, end-to-end, mean over 3 runs):

Case A (sticky=v2 always):
`p50=42  p95=61  p99=78`

Case B (sticky=v3, fallback per-batch if max_prefill>8192):
`p50=39  p95=58  p99=96`  <- p99 worse b/c mixed batches flip kernels

Case C (force v3 only, no fallback):
`p50=38  p95=56  p99=79`  <- looks good *until* you run pure 16k/24k, then we saw occasional kernel error in one run (might be harness issue)

Sofia Ivanova: This is basically scheduler + kernel interaction. If we bucket long-prefill separately (>=8k) we can avoid contaminating the short batches.

We already have workload buckets in scheduler; we can add a “long_ctx_prefill” bucket and prevent mixing those into the same prefill batch.

Noah Patel: that’s the right direction. Kernel selection should be mostly stable; scheduler should reduce the need for per-batch fallback.

Hiro Tanaka: agreed but we still need a safe kernel rule for the long_ctx bucket. Do we want v2 always for >8192? or can we extend v3 to 16k?

Grace Kim: I did a quick single-stream microbench yesterday on v3 at longer contexts (same box):

```
prefill=8192  decode=64   v2=~2900 tok/s  v3=~3200 tok/s
prefill=12288 decode=64   v2=~2500 tok/s  v3=~2700 tok/s
prefill=16384 decode=64   v2=~2200 tok/s  v3=~2350 tok/s
```

No errors in that microbench.

But the fallback was added b/c we saw instability on a different model config (odd head dims / kv heads) and on CUDA 12.2.

Yuki Sato: so maybe the gate should be:
- compat gate (sku + cuda/driver) at model init
- allow v3 even if model max >8192
- runtime fallback only if (prefill_len > v3_max_prefill) OR if model config is known-bad

and for now set `v3_max_prefill=8192` in default profile until we validate 16k in benchmark-lab.

Omar El-Sayed: if we do this, pls make fallback reason super explicit.

Right now we only have `kernel_choice` and it’s hard to tell if we’re falling back due to “long prefill” vs “cuda too old” vs “model config blacklist”.

Proposed reasons:
- `compat_cuda_driver`
- `model_config_unsupported`
- `prefill_len_exceeded`
- `batch_max_prefill_exceeded`
- `runtime_error`

Hiro Tanaka: +1. Also please make sure we *don’t* evaluate `model.max_seq_len` as a hard block anymore. That should be at most a warning.

Marcus Reed: from perf gating POV, I’m nervous about changing kernel conditions without also changing scheduler, otherwise we’ll just regress p99 for mixed workloads.

Sofia Ivanova: I can take an action item to prototype a simple split:
- if request prefill_len >= 8192 -> route to separate prefill queue (no mixing)
- keep decode shared

Would be behind a profile flag so we can enable only for H100 initially.

Noah Patel: that’s good. One nuance: continuous batching for decode also depends on KV cache state; long-context requests will have bigger KV, so we might want separate decode admission control too. but let’s not scope creep.

Grace Kim: Implementation proposal on kernel side:
1) Change sticky selection logic to ignore `model_max_seq_len` (don’t disqualify v3)
2) Add per-request *hard fallback* based on actual `prefill_len` (not per batch) BUT if we can’t mix kernels within a batch, it effectively becomes per-batch anyway.
3) Add config knob in profile: `attn_v3_max_prefill` default 8192
4) Export `kernel_fallback_total{reason=...}`

If scheduler splits long prefill into separate batches, per-batch fallback shouldn’t hurt tail for normal traffic.

Isabella Rossi: +1. Also: the current gate uses `>= 8192` not `> 8192` in one spot, so 8192 exactly flips. Minor but shows up in my sweep. Probably should be consistent.

Hiro Tanaka: ok, decision for now:
- Remove “model max seqlen” as a disqualifier for v3.
- Keep conservative `attn_v3_max_prefill=8192` default; revisit 16k after benchmark-lab + stability.
- Scheduler to isolate >=8k prefill so mixed batches don’t create p99 spikes.
- Add fallback reason counters.

Grace: can you push a patch + tag me/Yuki/Omar?

Grace Kim: yep, I’ll open a PR today. Will include a log at startup like:
`attn_kernel=v3 compat_ok=true v3_max_prefill=8192`.

Omar El-Sayed: ty. also please make sure `/health` debug endpoint shows `active_attn_kernel` + `v3_max_prefill` once it lands (oncall asks constantly).

Marcus Reed: once PR is up, I’ll run the mixed distribution case in benchmark-lab to validate p99.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll start a small diff on scheduler bucket split and link here. Might take me a day.

Yuki Sato: :thumbsup: thanks all. this one will definitely matter for Dedicated customers doing 16k/32k contexts but mostly short queries.

Hiro Tanaka: keeping thread open. Isabella, if you can drop the raw csv/log excerpt showing the current `model_max_seq_len` gate firing, that’ll help the PR review.
